title: When Automatic Captions Get a Name Wrong
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript: At a small archive, volunteers were preparing recorded interviews for a public exhibition. An automatic captioning system saved time, but it often confused the names of local streets with more common words. To see whether that mattered to visitors, the archive prepared two versions of the same clips. One kept the original captions. In the other, a volunteer corrected only place names, leaving the rest of the text untouched. Visitors watched one version and tried to find the places mentioned on a paper map. Those who saw the corrected names located more streets, although the two groups recalled a similar number of facts about the interviews. The archive now checks names first when preparing captions. Its study did not include people who rely entirely on written captions, so the team still needs to learn what other errors might affect that audience.

questions.prompt: Which kind of caption error prompted the study?
options: Entire sentences appearing out of order.
Local street names being replaced by familiar words.
questions.answer: Local street names being replaced by familiar words.
questions.explanation: 自动字幕常把当地街道名称误写成更常见的单词。

questions.prompt: What advantage did the corrected captions give visitors?
options: They could find more streets on the map.
They could finish listening to the clips sooner.
questions.answer: They could find more streets on the map.
questions.explanation: 看更正版本的访客能在地图上找到更多街道，但两组记住的事实数量相近。
